source: 1968 English primary book; draft faithful restatements, awaiting detailed verification

problems.problem: Choose terms from the harmonic series so that the sum of the chosen terms is finite. Prove that the selected terms have density zero within the harmonic sequence $1,\frac12,\frac13,\ldots$.
Consider the iterates $x_{n+1}=f(x_n)$ for $n\ge0$, with $x_0\in[0,1]$ and $f(x)=4x-4x^2$. Determine all starting points $x_0$ for which $(x_n)$ converges and find its limit.

In lawn tennis, a player wins a game upon scoring at least four points and at least two more than the opponent. A player wins a set upon winning at least six games and at least two more than the opponent. What is the minimum possible percentage of all points scored by the winner of a set?
Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial satisfying $f(0)=0$ and such that $\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$ is an integer for any distinct integers $a,b$. Can such a polynomial have a coefficient that is not an integer?
Let $n>3$ be an integer. Prove that the least common multiple of all products $x_1x_2\cdots x_k$, where $k\ge1$, the $x_i$ are positive integers and $x_1+\cdots+x_k\le n$, is less than $n!$.

For any positive integers $n,r$, prove that there exists a polynomial $f(x)$ of degree $n$ with integer coefficients such that every polynomial $g(x)$ of degree at most $n$ for which all coefficients of $f(x)-g(x)$ are integers of absolute value at most $r$ is irreducible over $\mathbb Q$.
How many nonzero terms occur in the expansion of a determinant of order $2n$ if precisely those entries $a_{ik}$ with $i-k$ divisible by $n$ are nonzero?
For which finite commutative groups is the product of all group elements equal to the identity element?

Let $\alpha$ be a projective plane and $c$ a closed polygon in $\alpha$. Prove that $c$ divides $\alpha$ into two regions if and only if there is a straight line $g$ in $\alpha$ having an even number of intersection points with $c$.
Determine all convex polyhedra with no diagonals, meaning that every line segment joining two vertices lies on the boundary of the polyhedron.
Can three conics in the plane be chosen so that every line intersects at least two of them and through every point of the plane there pass tangents to at least two of them?
Let $G$ be a noncommutative group. Show that the set of automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of $G$ forms a group containing the automorphism group as a direct factor.
Choose a pairing of $2n$ distinct points on a circle uniformly at random among all pairings, and draw the corresponding $n$ chords. Find the probability that no two of these chords intersect.

Place $32$ white and $32$ black chessmen on a chessboard. Two chessmen of different colours are called related if they occupy a common row or column. Find the maximum and minimum possible number of related pairs.
Show that every closed curve on the unit sphere of length less than $2\pi$ lies entirely in some closed hemisphere.
Prove that every positive integer has at least as many positive divisors of the form $3k+1$ as divisors of the form $3k-1$.

A point performs a random walk on a triangular lattice in the plane, moving at each step with equal probability along any of the six lattice directions. Prove that it returns to its starting point with probability $1$ if the walk is continued indefinitely.
Determine all finite groups that have exactly one proper maximal subgroup.

Given a triangle $ABC$, construct externally on its sides similar isosceles triangles $ABC_1$, $BCA_1$, $CAB_1$. Prove that the lines $AA_1$, $BB_1$, $CC_1$ are concurrent. Does the analogous claim hold in elliptic or hyperbolic geometry?
Show that a ring $R$ is commutative if $x^2-x$ belongs to the centre of $R$ for every $x\in R$.
Prove that every tetrahedron has three acute dihedral angles whose incident faces together include all four faces of the tetrahedron.

Show that a convex polyhedron with congruent faces and a vertex set of regular distribution is regular. Here regular distribution means that for any two vertices an isometry preserving the vertex set maps one to the other.
Find the minimum of $\max\{|1+z|,|1+z^2|\}$ over all complex numbers $z$.
Find the number of triangulations of a convex $n$-gon, and the number of triangulations in which each triangle has at least one side on the boundary of the original polygon.
Prove that a convex polyhedron has an even number of faces if every face is centrally symmetric.
